sections.title: English
sections.detail: Candidates are expected to have basic knowledge of English grammar, parts of speech, prepositions, punctuation, active and passive voice, idioms, proverbs, phrases, synonyms, antonyms, analogies, sentence construction etc. Candidates should be able to use English correctly.

sections.title: Urdu
sections.detail: The candidates are expected to have a good command over the Urdu language, its correct usage, grammar, idioms, and proverbs etc.

sections.title: Islamic Studies (General Knowledge for non-Muslim candidates)
sections.detail: The candidates are expected to display basic knowledge of the Holy Quran, Hadith, life and times of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), Khulafa-e-Rashideen, Pillars of Islam, Basic Beliefs, broad knowledge of important events in Islamic History and prominent personalities. Moreover, Non-Muslim candidates have the option either to attempt questions on Islamic Studies or the questions pertaining to general knowledge.

subjects.title: Botany

topics.title: Cryptogamic Botany
topics.detail: Algae: Classification (Fritsch, Bold & Wynne), Major algal groups (Cyanophyta, Chlorophyta, Charophyta, Bacillariophyta, Phaeophyta, Rhodophyta), thallus organization, pigments, reserve food, life cycles (Isomorphic, Heteromorphic, Diplontic, Triphasic). Economic importance (agar, alginate, biofertilizers). Algal blooms. Fungi: Classification (Ainsworth), Major fungal groups (Phycomycetes, Ascomycetes, Basidiomycetes, Deuteromycetes), cell wall, hyphal modifications, reproduction. Lichens; mycorrhizae (Ectomycorrhizae vs Endomycorrhizae). Plant diseases & control. Bryophytes: Liverworts, Hornworts, Mosses – comparative study. Alternation of generations, apogamy, apospory.

topics.title: Pteridophytes & Gymnosperms
topics.detail: Pteridophytes: Psilopsida, Lycopsida, Sphenopsida, Pteropsida. Heterospory & seed habit. Gymnosperms: Cycadales, Ginkgoales, Coniferales, and Gnetales– their structure, life history, affinities. Seed structure & ontogeny. Economic importance.

topics.title: Plant Anatomy & Embryology
topics.detail: Anatomy: Meristems (apical meristems and the tunica-corpus theory). Tissue systems. Vascular cambium & secondary growth (dicot stem/root). Anomalous secondary growth. Leaf, stem, root anatomy. Embryology: Microsporogenesis, Megasporogenesis. Anther & ovule types. Pollination, fertilization, double fertilization. Embryo & endosperm development. Polyembryony, apomixis.

topics.title: Taxonomy of Angiosperms
topics.detail: Systematics: Bentham & Hooker, Engler & Prantl, Takhtajan, Cronquist, APG. ICBN/ICN rules. Taxonomic hierarchy. Herbarium & botanical gardens. Modern Trends: Biosystematics, Chemotaxonomy, Numerical Taxonomy, Molecular Taxonomy. Families: Fabaceae, Solanaceae, Poaceae, Asteraceae, Liliaceae–their diagnostic characters and economic importance.

topics.title: Plant Physiology & Biochemistry
topics.detail: Water relations: Water potential (Ψw = Ψs + Ψp + Ψg) and its components; water absorption; transpiration; and stomatal regulation. Phloem transport (Pressure-Flow Hypothesis). Mineral Nutrition: Macro/micronutrients, deficiency symptoms, active/passive transport. Photosynthesis and respiration: Light-dependent reactions (Z-scheme), Calvin cycle, C3/C4/CAM/pathways, photorespiration, and celluar respiration including glycolysis, the Krebs cycle, the electron transport chain (ETC), and oxidative phosphorylation. Plant hormones: Auxins, gibberellins acids (GAs), cytokinins, abscisic acid (ABA), and ethylene. Photoperiodism, Vernalization, Dormancy, Germination.

sections.title: SECTION B: APPLIED, MOLECULAR & ENVIRONMENTAL BOTANY

topics.title: Ecology & Environmental Biology
topics.detail: Factors: Climatic (Light, Temperature, Wind), Edaphic (Soil), Biotic. Population & Community Ecology: Sampling (Quadrat, Line intercept), Ecological characteristics, Succession. Ecosystem ecology: Components, food chains, food webs, ecological pyramids, and biogeochemical cycles including the hydrological (water) and the nitrogen cycle. Applied Ecology: Soil salinity & water logging in Pakistan – causes & reclamation. Deforestation, Biodiversity conservation, Pollution.

topics.title: Cytology & Genetics
topics.detail: Cytology: Cell cycle, Mitosis, Meiosis. Ultra-structure of organelles (Mitochondria, Golgi, ER, Plastids, Ribosomes, Nucleus). Chromosomal aberrations; aneuploidy, euploidy, inversions, and translocations. Genetics: Mendelian laws of segregation and independent assortment; backcross and test crosses. Dominance, Incomplete dominance. Sex- linked inheritance. Linkage & Crossing over. Multiple alleles, Epistasis.

topics.title: Molecular Biology & Biotechnology
topics.detail: Molecular biology: DNA as the hereditary material; DNA replication; transcription; the genetic code; and translation. Regulation of gene expression (lac operon). Biotechnology: Genetic engineering, genetically modified organisms (GMOs), tissue culture, and applications in agriculture and medicine.

topics.title: Evolution
topics.detail: Concepts and history of evolution; convergent, divergent, and parallel evolution; natural selection; origin and the first plant cell; evolution of organized plant structures; and early aquatic and terrestrial ecosystems.

topics.title: Applied & Economic Botany
topics.detail: Economic importance of plants: Cereals, Pulses, Oilseeds, Fibers, Medicinal Plants, Timber, Fruits. Ethnobotany in Pakistan. Conservation strategies.

children.detail: Introduction and Fundamental Concepts of Business Economics, Basic Economics Tools, Optimization Techniques, Demand Analysis and Forecasting, Production and Cost Analysis, Market Structure and Pricing policies, Macroeconomic Environment and Business.

children.title: Principles Of Auditing
children.detail: Introduction and Nature of Auditing, Difference between Accounting and Auditing, Introduction to Audit Classification, Steps before Commencement of Audit, Internal Control and Risk Assessment, Verification of Assets, Audit Procedures and Evidence, Techniques for Gathering Documentation, Audit Reporting.

children.title: Taxation Management
children.detail: Introduction and Scope of Income Tax Law in Pakistan, Basic Terminologies of Income Tax, Income Exempt from Tax, Income From Salary, Income from Business and Profession, Income from Property, Income from Capital Gains, Income from Other Sources, Capital and Revenue Receipts, Capital and Revenue Expenditures, Calculations of Tax Payable.

children.title: Management
children.detail: Management History, Planning, Goals and Plans, Contemporary Issues in Planning. Organizational Structure, Traditional Organizational Designs, Organizing, Motivation, Leading, Controlling.

children.title: Trade Policies And Regulatory Framework
children.detail: Foundations of International Trade Policy, Instruments of Trade Policy, Trade Theories, Economic Integration, World Trade Organization (WTO), International Financial Institutions, Regional Trade Agreements (RTAs), Pakistan’s Trade and Commercial Policy Framework, Trade Documents and Procedures, Corporate Regulations, Competition Laws, Intellectual Property Rights.

children.title: Computers and Computing
children.detail: Computers and Computing: History and evolution of computing, stages of computing, basic machine structure, the Von Neumann model, types of computers (supercomputer, mainframe, mini and microcomputers), and Computer Based Information Systems (CBIS).

children.title: Number Systems and Logic
children.detail: Number Systems and Logic: Representation of numbers, binary arithmetic, data representations, number base conversions, Boolean algebra, and basic operations at machine level.

children.title: Hardware, I/O and Storage
children.detail: Hardware, I/O and Storage: Processor structure and memory structures (difference between primary and secondary memory, RAM and cache memory), input devices (keyboard, pointing devices, data acquisition devices), output devices (monitor, printer, plotter), storage media (hard disk drives, optical drives, flash drives, RAID arrays), and computer security and virus protection.

children.title: System Software and Operating Systems
children.detail: System Software and Operating Systems: Differences between system software and application software, functions of the operating system, architecture of personal, server, and mobile operating systems, command line interface (Linux command line interface, file management and redirection), and utilities.

children.title: Office Automation
children.detail: Office Automation: Microsoft Office package functionalities (formatting in Word, formulas in Excel, presentation slides in PowerPoint, database in Access), and office automation through Google Workspace, OneDrive, Dropbox and note-taking applications.

children.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking
children.detail: Data Communication and Computer Networking: Data communication model, analog and digital data communication, modems, transmission media, network topologies (star, bus, ring), LANs/WANs, network protocols, evolution of the Internet, browsers and search engines.

children.title: ICT Applications and Emerging Technologies
children.detail: ICT Applications and Emerging Technologies: ICT applications in learning (LMS, online learning), health and well-being (telemedicine, wearable devices), personal finance management (electronic wallet, e-commerce), and artificial intelligence in brief, and software engineering.

children.title: ICT Citizenship and Ethics
children.detail: ICT Citizenship and Ethics: Issues of intellectual property and copyright, preventing plagiarism, data integrity, managing misinformation and fake news, and social aspects of computing.

children.title: Introduction to Networking and Network Architectures
children.detail: Introduction to Networking and Network Architectures: Concepts in networking, network topologies, protocol architecture and network system architecture (OSI and TCP/IP reference model) with considerations that apply.

children.title: The Physical Layer and Transmission Concepts
children.detail: The Physical Layer and Transmission Concepts: Analog and digital transmissions, transmission mediums, noise considerations, encoding schemes, multiplexing and asynchronous and synchronous transmissions.

children.title: The Data Link Layer and Local Area Networks
children.detail: The Data Link Layer and Local Area Networks: Error Control, Flow Control, Data Link Protocols (HDLC, PPP), MAC addressing, access schemes and Local Area Network Technologies (Ethernet, Token Ring).

children.title: The Network Layer and Internetworking
children.detail: The Network Layer and Internetworking: Circuit Switching and Packet Switching, Bridging, Internetworking and Routing, IP addresses (IPv4 and IPv6), Subnetting and CIDR, and routing protocols.

children.title: The Transport Layer
children.detail: The Transport Layer: Transport layer protocols (TCP, UDP), Ports and sockets, connection setup and teardown, and Flow and congestion control.

children.title: The Application Layer and Current Issues
children.detail: The Application Layer and Current Issues: Application layer protocols (HTTP, DNS, SMTP, FTP) and current issues in software defined networks and Computer Networks.

children.title: Network Security and Programming Exercises
children.detail: Network Security and Programming Exercises: Network security issues, cryptography basics, firewall concepts, and programming assignments dealing with networking, routing, switching and protocols implementation.

children.title: Introduction and Architecture
children.detail: Introduction and Architecture: Fundamentals of problem solving, algorithms, pseudo code, flowcharting, and Von Neumann computer architecture.

children.title: Language Fundamentals and I/O
children.detail: Language Fundamentals and I/O: Compilation and linking of programs; data types; variables; type casting; memory concepts; and input output constructs.

children.title: Operators and Expressions
children.detail: Operators and Expressions: Arithmetic operators, relational operators, logical operators, equality operators, precedence of operators, and integer division.

children.title: Control Structures
children.detail: Control Structures: Selection constructs (if, else, switch), Structured Programming Theorem, and repetition constructs (while, do while, for).

children.title: Modular Programming
children.detail: Modular Programming: Functions; scope rules; passing arguments by value and by reference; stack frame creation and destruction; recursion; and random numbers.

children.title: Data Structures (Arrays and Lists)
children.detail: Data Structures (Arrays and Lists): One-dimensional arrays/lists; multidimensional arrays/lists; memory organization; searching and sorting; and strings and string manipulations.

children.title: Advanced Data Types
children.detail: Advanced Data Types: Structures, typedef, unions; pointers; pointer arithmetic; function pointers; and references.

children.title: Memory and File Management
children.detail: Memory and File Management: Static and dynamic memory allocation (new / delete); file streams (input/ output); sequential and random file access; and preprocessor directives.

children.title: Introduction and Complexity Analysis
children.detail: Introduction and Complexity Analysis: The roles of data structures and algorithms, abstract data type (ADT), OOP, and asymptotic complexity, including Big-O notation and the analysis of best, average and worst-case scenarios.

children.title: Linear Data Structures
children.detail: Linear Data Structures: Arrays, linear lists, singly and doubly and circular linked lists, sorted lists, stacks, queues, deques and priority queue, and their practical applications such as bracket checking, expression conversion, and scheduling.

children.title: Recursion and Sorting Algorithms
children.detail: Recursion and Sorting Algorithms: Direct recursion and recursive tracing and divide and conquer approaches, along with the discussion on different sorting algorithms like bubble sort, selection sort, insertion sort, merge sort, quick sort, heap sort, shell sort, radix sort and bucket sort.

children.title: Searching and Hashing
children.detail: Searching and Hashing: Linear and binary search, hash functions, hash collision resolution, open addressing, chaining and indexing.

children.title: Advanced Trees
children.detail: Advanced Trees: Binary tree, tree traversal, binary search tree (BST), balanced tree (AVL trees, M-way trees) and heaps.

children.title: Graph and Advanced Applications
children.detail: Graph and Advanced Applications: Graph representations (Adjacency matrix and adjacency list), BFS, DFS, shortest path, minimum spanning trees, topological sort, cycle detection, graph coloring and data compression using Huffman coding.

children.title: Introduction to Operating Systems and System Structures
children.detail: Introduction to Operating Systems and System Structures: History and Evolution, Classification of Operating Systems, System Components, System Services, Dual Mode Operation, Protection from Hardware/ Memory/ I/O, System Call Interface and Virtual Machines.

children.title: Processes and Threads
children.detail: Processes and Threads: Concept of Processes, Process Control Block, States of Process, Process Scheduling, Process Creation and Process Termination (fork(), wait(), exec()), Multi-Threading Models, Threading Issues and Thread Libraries (Pthreads).

children.title: CPU Scheduling
children.detail: CPU Scheduling: Criteria for Scheduling, Pre-Emptive and Non-Pre-Emptive Algorithms (FCFS, SJF, SRTF, Priority, Round Robin, MLQ, MLFQ), Thread Scheduling, Multiprocessor Scheduling.

children.title: Process Synchronization and Concurrency
children.detail: Process Synchronization and Concurrency: Race Condition, Critical Section Problem, Software & Hardware Solutions to critical section problem (Peterson’s Solution and Test-and-Set lock), Mutex Locks, Semaphores, Classical Problems in Synchronization (Producer – Consumer Problem, Dining Philosophers Problem, Reader – Writer Problem) Monitors.

children.title: Deadlock
children.detail: Deadlock: System Model, Deadlock Characteristics, Four Necessary Conditions of Deadlock, Resource Allocation Graphs, Deadlock Prevention & Avoidance (Banker’s Algorithm), Deadlock Detection & Recovery.

children.title: Memory Management
children.detail: Memory Management: Address Binding, Logical Addresses vs Physical Addresses, Contiguous Memory Allocation (Text Segment, Data Segment, Heap Segment, MFT, MVT; Fragmentation), Paging, Page Tables and Hierarchical Inverted Page Tables, Segmentation and Paged Segmentation.

children.title: Virtual Memory
children.detail: Virtual Memory: Demand Paging, Performance of Virtual Memory, Page Replacement Algorithms (FIFO, OPTIMAL, LRU, LFU), Frame Allocation, Thrashing, Working Set Model, Memory Mapped Files.

children.title: Storage Management, File Systems and Security
children.detail: Storage Management, File Systems and Security: File Concept, Access Methods, Directory Structure and Disk Structure, Free-Space Management, Disk Scheduling Algorithms, RAIDs, File System Reliability and Protection, Security of Operating System.

children.title: Number Systems and Binary Arithmetic
children.detail: Number Systems and Binary Arithmetic: Numerical representation, number system conversions, data representations, Radix and Diminished Radix Complements and Binary Subtraction.

children.title: Boolean Algebra and Reduction of Boolean Functions
children.detail: Boolean Algebra and Reduction of Boolean Functions: Basic theorems and properties of Boolean algebra, Boolean functions, standard forms (canonical forms) (minterms and maxterms), reduction of Boolean functions (K-maps and QuineMcCluskey method).

children.title: Combinational Logic Circuits
children.detail: Combinational Logic Circuits: Design and analysis techniques, design of combinational circuits (using gates), adders, subtractors, converters, magnitude comparators, decoders, encoders, multiplexers and demultiplexers.

children.title: Sequential Logic Circuits
children.detail: Sequential Logic Circuits: Latches, Flip-Flops (SR, D, JK, T), Analysis of clocked sequential circuits, State reduction and assignment, registers and Shift Registers.

children.title: Synchronous and Asynchronous State Machines
children.detail: Synchronous and Asynchronous State Machines: Ripple and synchronous counters, timing sequences, Mealy and Moore Finite State Machines.

children.title: Memory Units and Programmable Logic Devices
children.detail: Memory Units and Programmable Logic Devices: Random Access Memory (RAM), Read Only Memory (ROM), Programmable Logic Arrays (PLA’s), CPLDs, FPGAs, logic families and digital integrated circuits.

children.title: Hardware Description Languages and Circuit Simulations
children.detail: Hardware Description Languages and Circuit Simulations: Overview of hardware description language (Verilog HDL/VHDL) and electronic design automation tools for digital logic simulation (MultiSim, SPICE or similar).

children.title: Introduction and Process Models
children.detail: Introduction and Process Models: The nature of software engineering, the motivations behind software engineering, and professional software engineering. Traditional process models (Linear sequential, Prototyping, RAD, Incremental, Spiral) as well as Agile software development process frameworks are covered.

children.title: Requirements Engineering
children.detail: Requirements Engineering: Concepts of requirements elicitation and analysis, functional and non-functional requirements, and different perspectives on modeling such as context, interaction, structure and behavior as well as requirement tracing.

children.title: Analysis and Modeling (structured and object-oriented)
children.detail: Analysis and Modeling (structured and object-oriented): Structured analysis (Data Flow Diagrams, State Transition Diagrams), UML modeling (Use Cases modeling, Activity Diagrams, Interaction Diagrams, Domain Modeling).

children.title: Architectural and Component Level Design
children.detail: Architectural and Component Level Design: Architectural design patterns, Data design, component level design, User Interface Design and GRASP (Cohesion, Coupling, Information Expert, Creator, Controller, Polymorphism).

children.title: Software Verification, Validation and Testing
children.detail: Software Verification, Validation and Testing: Software verification and validation approaches, criteria for measuring software correctness, efficiency and performance as well as technical reviews and the basics of software testing and test planning.

children.title: Project Management and Evolution
children.detail: Project Management and Evolution: Software evolution, project planning and management, configuration management, software process improvement and software reliability and performance standards.

children.title: Introduction and File Systems
children.detail: Introduction and File Systems: Comparison of file systems vs database systems, data redundancy, structural data dependency, database environment, three-schema architecture, and data independence.

children.title: Data Models and E-R Modeling
children.detail: Data Models and E-R Modeling: Survey of data models (Hierarchical, Network, Relational, Object-oriented) and ER modeling.

children.title: Relational Model and Relational Algebra
children.detail: Relational Model and Relational Algebra: Concepts related to relations, attributes, tuples, domains, keys, integrity constraints, and relational algebra operations (Selection, Projection, Cartesian product and Joins).

children.title: SQL
children.detail: SQL: Data Definition Language (DDL), Data Manipulation Language (DML), complex queries, subqueries, grouping and aggregation, views and security/authorization mechanisms.

children.title: Database Design and Normalization
children.detail: Database Design and Normalization: Functional dependencies, inference rules and normal forms (1NF, 2NF, 3NF, BCNF) within relational design.

children.title: Physical Storage and Indexing
children.detail: Physical Storage and Indexing: Storage structure, file organization, indexed files, hashed files, B-tree structure, dense and sparse indices, and database tuning.

children.title: Transactions, Concurrency Control, and Database Recovery
children.detail: Transactions, Concurrency Control, and Database Recovery: Atomicity, consistency, isolation and durability, transaction processing, concurrency control using locking, two phase locking, timestamps and optimistic concurrency control, deadlock and database recovery mechanisms.

children.title: Advanced and Emerging Databases
children.detail: Advanced and Emerging Databases: Distributed databases, data warehousing, data mining, and NoSQL.

children.title: Introduction and Intelligent Agents
children.detail: Introduction and Intelligent Agents: The definition of artificial intelligence, Turing test, rationality, PEAS, agent architectures, and some classical AI systems (General Problem Solver, ELIZA, OPS-5, Common Lisp)

children.title: Search Strategies and Adversarial Search
children.detail: Search Strategies and Adversarial Search: Uninformed search (Breadth-first search, Depth- limited search, Depth-first search, Iterative Deepening Search); Informed search (Greedy Best- first, A*), Local Search (Hill climbing, Simulated Annealing), Game Theory, Minimax Algorithm, Alpha-Beta Pruning

children.title: Knowledge Representation and Logic
children.detail: Knowledge Representation and Logic: Propositional and Predicate Logic, Rule-Based Systems, Semantic Networks, Frames, Objects, Scripts, Forward and Backward Chaining, Resolution, Unification, Logic Programming (Prolog)

children.title: Symbolic Mathematics and Probabilistic Reasoning
children.detail: Symbolic Mathematics and Probabilistic Reasoning: Symbolic mathematics problem solvers (Macsyma, PRESS); Management of Uncertainty, Bayes' Rule, Naive Bayes models, Fuzzy sets, Genetic Algorithms.

children.title: Foundations of Machine Learning
children.detail: Foundations of Machine Learning: Types of learning, Learning from Examples, Decision Trees, Linear Regression, Classification, Clustering, Evaluation Techniques.

children.title: Neural Networks and Deep Learning
children.detail: Neural Networks and Deep Learning: Perceptron, Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), Backpropagation, and shift from classic architecture to deep learning and neural networks.

children.title: Generative AI, Large Language Models, and Natural Language Processing (NLP)
children.detail: Generative AI, Large Language Models, and Natural Language Processing (NLP): NLP, Transformer Architecture (self-attention), Tokenization, Pre-training, Fine-Tuning, RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation), Vector Databases, Prompt Engineering (few-shot learning and chain-of-thought).

children.title: AI Ethics, Safety and Future Trends
children.detail: AI Ethics, Safety and Future Trends: Bias in models, Deepfakes, AI Privacy, Professional Ethics, Safety Alignment, Agentic Workflows (AutoGPT, considerations towards AGI).

children.title: Microeconomics
children.detail: Microeconomics: Meaning of microeconomics. Choice, scarcity and opportunity cost. Production Possibility Frontier. Goals of microeconomic policy: efficiency and equity.

children.title: Market economy
children.detail: Market economy: Demand, Supply and Price determination. Individual and market demand. Changes in demand. Individual and market supply. Changes in supply. Market equilibrium and impact of changes in demand and supply on market equilibrium. Elasticity of Supply and Demand. Point and Arc elasticity. Price, income and cross elasticities. Application of the concept of elasticity.

children.title: The Theory of Consumer Behaviour
children.detail: The Theory of Consumer Behaviour: Concept of utility and derivation of Demand curve. Cardinal and ordinal Utility. Consumer’s Surplus. Indifference Curves and their shapes. Marginal rate of substitution and convexity of Indifference Curves. The budget constraint and the equilibrium of the consumer. Income-Consumption and the Engel’s Curve. Price- consumption and Demand curve. Income and Substitution effects of a price change, the Hicksian method and the Slutsky method. Identification of normal goods, inferior goods and Giffen goods.

children.title: The Theory of Production
children.detail: The Theory of Production: The concepts of production cost and profit. Production function. The law of variable proportions. Cost curves in the short run and in the long run. Choice of input mix. The principle of Substitution. Isoquants, iso-cost line and the condition for cost minimization. The expansion path and returns to scale. Economies of scale. The very long run and the endogenous technical change.

children.title: Market Structures and Behaviour of firms. Perfectly competitive markets. Assumptions of the model. The supply curve of a firm and an industry in the short run. Short run and the…
children.detail: Market Structures and Behaviour of firms. Perfectly competitive markets. Assumptions of the model. The supply curve of a firm and an industry in the short run. Short run and the long run equilibrium of the firm and industry. The shape of the long run industry supply curve and the effects of changing technology. The allocative efficiency of perfect competition. Monopoly: Shape of the demand curve under monopoly. Elasticity of the demand curve and its implication for a monopolist. Short run and long run equilibrium. Price discrimination and its consequences. Analysis of price discrimination between markets. Dumping. Cartels as monopolies. The allocative inefficiency of monopoly. Comparison between perfect competition and monopoly. Imperfectly competitive market structures: Monopolistic competition. The concept of industry and group. Short run and long run equilibrium of a firm. Excess capacity. Comparison with perfect competition and monopoly. Oligopoly and its basic dilemma. Duopoly. Models of Non-collusive oligopoly: Cournot’s duopoly model, Chamberlain’s oligopoly model, Sweezy’s kinked-demand model. Collusive Oligopoly. Cartels: Joint profit maximization and market sharing cartels. Price leadership models. Mergers.

children.title: The Theory of Factor Pricing
children.detail: The Theory of Factor Pricing: Demand and Supply of inputs. Input demand in the short run and in the long run. The firms demand curve. The firm‟s demand curve for a single variable input. The industry‟s demand curve for an input. Elasticity of demand for inputs. The supply of inputs. Determination of price, quantity and income of an input. Monopsony.

children.title: What is Macroeconomics?
children.detail: What is Macroeconomics?: Major macroeconomic issues. Economic models. Stocks and flows, National income accounting, circular flow of income, real versus nominal GDP, the GDP deflator, the consumer price index, economic growth, actual versus potential output, business cycles and their phases, definition of full employment, unemployment, GDP gap, Inflation.

children.title: Classical Macroeconomics
children.detail: Classical Macroeconomics: The classical revolution, production, employment, labour demand and labour supply. Equilibrium output and employment. The quantity theory of money. The Cambridge approach to the Quantity theory. Aggregate Demand and Aggregate Supply in the classical system. The classical theory of rate of interest. Complete classical model and classical dichotomy.

children.title: The Keynesian Macroeconomics
children.detail: The Keynesian Macroeconomics: Aggregate expenditure and its components. Consumption function and Savings function. Investment and the real rate of interest. The equilibrium GDP in a closed economy simple multiplier. Government spending and taxes. Tax multiplier. GDP in an open economy. The net export function and the foreign trade multiplier. The augmented saving-investment approach. Fiscal and monetary policies.

children.title: Investment and its Determinants
children.detail: Investment and its Determinants: Marginal efficiency of capital and optimal capital stock, the marginal efficiency of investment. The stock market and Tobin‟s q-theory. Inventory investment and the accelerator model. The interaction of multiplier and accelerator. The derivation of IS curve and its slope. Factors that shift the IS curve.

children.title: The Money Market and LM-curve
children.detail: The Money Market and LM-curve. Keynes Theory of Liquidity preference. Supply of money. Monetary equilibrium and the rate of interest. Derivation of LM-curve and its slope. Factors that shift the LM curve. Keynes liquidity trap. Interaction of IS-LM curves. Adjustment to equilibrium in the IS-LM curve model. The algebra of the IS-LM model.

children.title: Aggregate Demand and Aggregate Supply
children.detail: Aggregate Demand and Aggregate Supply: Macroeconomic equilibrium in the short run. The effect of aggregate demand and aggregate supply shocks on the price level and GDP. Long run consequences of aggregate demand shocks. Long run aggregate supply curve. Inflationary and recessionary gaps. The theory of fiscal stabilization and its effectiveness. Transmission mechanism. Comparison of the Classical and Keynesian models and policy conclusions.

children.title: Inflation and Unemployment
children.detail: Inflation and Unemployment: Types of inflation, Supply shock and demand shock. Inflation as a monetary phenomenon. Stagflation. The theory of Phillips curve. The short run and the long run Phillips curve. The expectations augmented Phillips curve. Adaptive expectations. Unemployment. Frictional, structural and cyclical unemployment. Okun’s law. Hysteresis and the natural rate hypotheses.

children.title: Consumption Theories and Their Implications
children.detail: Consumption Theories and Their Implications: Keynesian absolute income hypothesis, Simon Kuznets findings, Duesenbury‟s hypothesis, Permanent income hypothesis, life cycle hypothesis, Robert Hall and the random-walk hypothesis.

children.title: Equations
children.detail: Equations: Equation vs Identities. Solution of linear, Quadratic and simultaneous equations. Equilibrium analysis in Economics. Partial market equilibrium. Equilibrium in National Income.

children.title: Derivatives
children.detail: Derivatives: The concept of derivatives. Slope vs elasticity of a function. Rules of differentiation. The derivation of marginal quantities in Economics.

children.title: Maxima and Minima of Functions
children.detail: Maxima and Minima of Functions: Criteria for relative maxima and minima. Point of inflection. First order and second order condition. Problems of optimization in Economics. Profit, utility and revenue maximization. Cost minimization.

children.title: Measurement and mathematical description
children.detail: SI units, dimensions and dimensional consistency; scalars and vectors; significant figures; measurement uncertainty and interpretation of graphs and experimental data.

children.title: Classical mechanics and waves
children.detail: Density; gravity; position, velocity and acceleration; mass, momentum, force and energy; angular momentum and torque; work and power; conservation laws, oscillations and engineering applications.

children.title: Quantum mechanics and particle physics
children.detail: Planck’s constant, quanta and quantization; matrix and wave mechanics at an introductory level; quantum harmonic oscillator; quantum numbers and spin; wave function; wave-particle duality; zero-point energy; Pauli’s exclusion principle and Heisenberg’s uncertainty principle; fundamental forces; elementary particles, antimatter, quantum gravity and vacuum energy at conceptual level.

children.title: Relativity
children.detail: Principle of relativity; inertial frames and invariance; speed of light; length contraction and time dilation; rest mass and rest energy; gravity, general relativity and stress-energy tensor at conceptual level.

children.title: Optics
children.detail: Ray and wave optics; reflection, refraction and scattering; lenses, mirrors and prisms; diffraction, dispersion and polarization; aberrations, optical resolution and optical instruments.

children.title: Solid-state physics
children.detail: Amorphous and crystalline solids; crystal structures; free-electron model; valence and conduction bands, band gap, electron and hole excitation; superconductivity and crystal optics.

children.title: Chemical foundations
children.detail: Atomic structure, periodic trends, chemical bonding, stoichiometry and concentration calculations; acids, bases, pH and buffers.

children.title: Gases, liquids and solutions
children.detail: Boyle's law and Charles's law; gas constant; Dalton's partial-pressure law; Graham's diffusion law; kinetic theory and heat capacity of gases; vapour pressure and boiling point; surface tension, viscosity, refractive index, polarimetry, intermolecular and intramolecular forces; ideal and non-ideal solutions, Raoult's law and Henry's law, solubility curves and heat of solution.

children.title: Solid state and X-rays
children.detail: Crystalline structure and properties; production of X-rays and crystal-structure applications; heat capacities of solids.

children.title: Electrochemistry
children.detail: Electrolysis; electrolytic conductance and migration of ions; galvanic, reversible and irreversible cells; standard electrode potentials; electrochemical series, buffer solutions and engineering applications.

children.title: Thermochemistry and kinetics
children.detail: Heat of reaction, basic chemical equilibrium and factors affecting reaction rate.

children.title: Industrial chemistry
children.detail: Corrosion mechanisms and control; water hardness and treatment; fuels and combustion; lubricants; cement chemistry; environmental chemistry, chemical hazards and safety.

children.title: Basic analytical methods
children.detail: Titrimetry, spectrophotometry and chromatography: principles and interpretation at introductory level.

children.title: Circuit fundamentals
children.detail: Electrical potential; resistance, conductance, conductivity and impedance; Ohm's law; series and parallel circuits; practical resistors; work, power, energy and Joule's law; capacitance and capacitors in series/parallel; AC quantities. Network solution methods: Kirchhoff's laws; nodal and mesh analysis; source transformation; Thevenin, Norton and maximum-power-transfer theorems.

children.title: Electricity and magnetism
children.detail: Electric-field intensity and Gauss's theorem; capacitors, capacitance; capacitors in series and parallel; force on a current-carrying conductor; electric and magnetic circuits and leakage flux; Faraday's and Lenz's laws; induced emf/current; self and mutual inductance and series/parallel combinations; hysteresis; magnetic-field energy; generation of alternating voltage/current.

children.title: Machines and transformers
children.detail: DC shunt, series, and compound motors; speed-torque relations; single- and three-phase induction and synchronous motors; generators; transformers; principle, construction, ratios, connections, losses, performance and efficiency.

children.title: Electronics and digital systems
children.detail: n- and p-type materials; PN junctions and diodes; transistor types and basic circuit calculations; Class A/B and feedback amplifiers; RC oscillators; op-amps, timers, flip-flops, converters and filters. Digital logic and embedded systems: Number systems, Boolean logic, combinational/sequential circuits, microcontrollers and embedded-system concepts.

children.title: Communication, signals and control
children.detail: EM theory, antennas, gain, free-space loss and fading; AM, FM, PM, PWM, delta modulation, FSK, ASK and PSK; error correction, demodulation, detectors, transmitters and receivers; filters, Z-transform, S-domain, transfer functions, Nyquist criterion and stability.

children.title: Computing
children.detail: Computer evolution; CPU, storage, input/output and multimedia; operating systems and programming languages; networks and internet; systems analysis and design; MIS and e-commerce; security, privacy and professional ethics.

children.title: Power systems
children.detail: Network analysis; polyphase circuits; transients; transmission lines and losses. Protection, measurement and modern power: Electrical measurements, sensors and transducers; protection and earthing; electrical safety; power factor; introductory power electronics, renewable-energy integration and smart grids.

children.title: Engineering mechanics and strength of materials
children.detail: Force systems, equilibrium, friction, centroid and geometric properties; motion, work and energy; stress and strain; engineering and true stress/strain; elastic and plastic deformation; tensile testing and stress-strain curve; yield and ultimate strength; elongation, toughness, resilience, ductility and malleability; shear, bending, torsion, bending moment and principal stresses; Brinell and Rockwell hardness.

children.title: Fluid mechanics and machines
children.detail: Fluid properties; statics and dynamics; laminar and turbulent flow and Reynolds number; continuity, momentum and energy concepts; head loss; power transmission by fluids; pumps and turbines.

children.title: Thermodynamics and heat transfer
children.detail: Properties of fluids and steam; first and second laws; enthalpy, entropy and heat capacity; Carnot cycle; Gibbs free energy and equilibrium; PV diagrams; heat engines; two and four-stroke heat engines; steam turbines and power plants; refrigeration and air conditioning; conduction, convection and radiation; evaporators and condensers.

children.title: Manufacturing
children.detail: Casting, forging, rolling, extrusion, wire drawing, welding, machining, turning, milling, shaping, gear cutting, drilling and fitting.

children.title: Machine and production practices
children.detail: Basic machine elements and design considerations; metrology, limits, fits, tolerances and surface finish; engineering drawing and CAD/CAM, CNC and additive manufacturing concepts; instrumentation, condition monitoring, maintenance and workshop safety.

children.title: Structure of materials
children.detail: Classification of materials; atomic structure and metallic bonding; crystal structures and geometry. Crystal defects and diffusion: Point, line and surface defects; diffusion mechanisms and their engineering significance.

children.title: Metallic materials
children.detail: Mechanical properties of metals and alloys; ferrous and non-ferrous metals and alloys; industrial applications. Phase relations and heat treatment: Binary phase diagrams; iron-carbon system; phase transformations; annealing, normalizing, hardening and tempering.

children.title: Polymers, ceramics and glasses
children.detail: Polymerization; general-purpose and engineering thermoplastics, thermosets and rubbers; traditional and engineering ceramics; ceramic processing and electrical, mechanical and thermal properties; glasses.

children.title: Composites and advanced materials
children.detail: Particle-, fibre-, and laminate-reinforced composites; introductory nanomaterials, biomaterials and functional materials.

children.title: Behaviour, testing and selection
children.detail: Tensile, hardness, impact and fatigue concepts; fracture, creep, corrosion and wear; introductory optical and electron microscopy, and X-ray characterization; material selection based on performance, cost, safety and sustainability.

children.title: Structures
children.detail: Stress, strain, shearing force and bending moment; simply supported and cantilever beams; columns and footings; basic structural behaviour; pulleys and gears as elementary mechanics applications.

children.title: Civil engineering materials and construction
children.detail: Properties and uses of cement, aggregates, concrete, steel, bitumen and masonry; basic construction methods, estimation and quality control.

children.title: Surveying and geomatics
children.detail: Distance, angle and level measurement; traversing, contours and setting out; introductory total station, GNSS and GIS concepts.

children.title: Geotechnical engineering
children.detail: Soil classification, compaction, consolidation, permeability, shear strength, bearing capacity, settlement, soil improvement, and slope stability and its mitigation at an introductory level.

children.title: Transportation engineering
children.detail: Highway administration and scheme preparation; traffic and environmental appraisal; highway geometry, drainage, lighting, signing, communications and safety; urban roads and traffic; pavement materials and basics; maintenance and low-cost roads in developing countries.

children.title: Environmental engineering
children.detail: Environmental impacts of water-resource and transportation projects; water supply and distribution; wastewater treatment and management. Solid waste, pollution, and assessment: Municipal solid-waste management; air, noise and smog pollution basics; environmental-impact assessment and mitigation.

children.title: Hydraulics and water-resources engineering
children.detail: Fluid properties; pressure- and flow-measuring devices; pipeline losses; open channels; barrages and dams. Hydrology and resilience: Hydrologic cycle, rainfall-runoff and flood concepts; climate-resilient infrastructure, disaster-risk awareness and occupational safety.

children.title: Engineering Economy, Cost and Financial Management
children.detail: Cost classification and estimation; time value of money; simple and compound interest; cash-flow diagrams; present and future worth; Net Present Value (NPV)and Net Future Value (NFV); annual worth; internal rate of return; benefit-cost ratio; break-even analysis; budgeting; basic income statement and balance sheet; depreciation, inflation, replacement, life-cycle costing, financial risk and sensitivity analysis.

children.title: Project, Risk and Professional Management
children.detail: Project objectives and life cycle; scope and work-breakdown structure; timelines, milestones, dependencies and Gantt charts; CPM and PERT; resource and cost estimation; resource allocation and levelling; progress monitoring; project risk identification, assessment, response and control; procurement, contracts, stakeholders, communication, change control and closure.

children.title: Professional practices and work ethics
children.detail: management functions; teamwork and leadership; engineering ethics; public and environmental responsibility; occupational health and safety; technical communication and accountability.

children.title: Quality, reliability, and testing
children.detail: Quality planning, assurance, control and improvement; Deming, Juran and Crosby principles; quality circles; management responsibility; purchasing and design validation; test plans, execution, records and reports; destructive and non-destructive testing; inspection, sampling, acceptance criteria, calibration and measurement uncertainty; quality audit and corrective and preventive action.

children.title: Reliability and improvement tools
children.detail: PDCA; basic control charts and process capability; root-cause analysis; ISO 9001 concepts; failure modes; reliability, availability, maintainability, verification, validation and traceability.

children.title: Operations, Production, Inventory and Decision Tools:
children.detail: Production and operations management; manufacturing systems; process selection and optimization; time analysis and work study; resource and raw-material planning; capacity, scheduling and production control; inventory identification and systems; FIFO and LIFO as issue and valuation methods; problem analysis, decision-support systems, decision trees, design of experiments and management tools.

subjects.title: Mass Communication

sections.title: FOUNDATIONS OF MASS COMMUNICATION, COMMUNICATION THEORY AND MEDIA–SOCIETY RELATIONS
sections.detail: Introduction to Mass Communication; Communication Theories; Advanced Theories of Communication; Media and Society; Media and Information Literacy.

topics.title: Process and models of communication
topics.detail: Process and models of communication. Source–message–channel–receiver–noise–feedback and redundancy; types and levels (intrapersonal, interpersonal, group, organisational, mass); Shannon–Weaver, Lasswell, Schramm, Osgood, Berlo, Westley–MacLean, Gerbner and Dance models; movement from linear to transactional and networked models.

topics.title: Barriers and principles of effective communication
topics.detail: Barriers and principles of effective communication. Physical, semantic, psychological, cultural and technological barriers; principles of effective communication (clarity, completeness, conciseness, credibility, context, courtesy, feedback).

topics.title: Functions and nature of mass media
topics.detail: Functions and nature of mass media. Surveillance, interpretation, socialisation, entertainment and mobilisation; characteristics of mass audiences; mass communication and mass self-communication.

topics.title: Media effects and audience theories
topics.detail: Media effects and audience theories. Hypodermic needle/magic bullet model; two-step flow of communication and opinion leaders; limited-effects paradigm; agenda-setting, framing and priming; gatekeeping; spiral of silence; cultivation; uses and gratifications; media dependency; social learning; active and participatory audiences.

topics.title: Normative and critical perspectives
topics.detail: Normative and critical perspectives. Four Theories of the Press and their critiques; social-responsibility, development-media and democratic-participant theories; public sphere; Frankfurt School and the culture industry; hegemony; political economy of media; encoding/decoding; media imperialism; feminist and postcolonial critiques.

topics.title: Media, culture and society
topics.detail: Media, culture and society. Public opinion and propaganda; representation, stereotyping, gender and minorities; popular culture and consumerism; media and democracy; mediatisation of society.

topics.title: Media and information literacy
topics.detail: Media and information literacy. Access, analysis, evaluation and creation of media content; misinformation, disinformation and malinformation; propaganda techniques; fact-checking and verification; critical media consumption.

sections.title: MEDIA IN PAKISTAN: HISTORY, STRUCTURE, LAWS AND ETHICS

topics.title: Press of the Sub-Continent
topics.detail: Press of the Sub-Continent. Origins of the Urdu and English press; the role of Sir Syed Ahmed Khan, Maulana Zafar Ali Khan, Muhammad Ali Jauhar, Hasrat Mohani and Hameed Nizami; the press and the Pakistan Movement.

topics.title: Evolution of media in Pakistan
topics.detail: Evolution of media in Pakistan. Press after 1947; radio (Radio Pakistan, FM and community radio); television (PTV and the expansion of private satellite channels after 2002); internet and social media; ownership patterns and media groups.

topics.title: Organisational structures of newspapers and news agencies
topics.detail: Organisational structures of newspapers and news agencies. Editorial, news, production, circulation, advertising and management departments; APNS, CPNE and journalists’ unions; national and international news agencies.

topics.title: Government–media relationship

topics.title: Press laws and regulation

Articles 19 and 19A of the Constitution; Registration of Printing Presses and Publications Ordinance 1988; Press Council of Pakistan Ordinance 2002; PEMRA Ordinance 2002; Defamation Ordinance 2002; contempt of court; Right of Access to Information Act 2017; Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (PECA) 2016; Protection of Journalists and Media Professionals Act 2021 (all as amended).

topics.title: Contemporary challenges
topics.detail: Contemporary challenges. Economic pressures, digital disruption, political and commercial influence, polarisation and disinformation.

children.title: Research Methodology

children.title: Social Stratification

children.title: Family & Marriage

topics.title: Descriptive Statistics
topics.detail: Meaning of Statistics, its characteristics, uses and misuses of statistics, observations and variables, types of variables, data and its types according to nature (qualitative and quantitative), w.r.t. source (primary and secondary), measurement scales (nominal, ordinal, interval and ratio), population and sample, descriptive and inferential statistics, description of qualitative and quantitative data using frequency tables and graphs (simple bar chart, histogram, pie chart, stem and leaf plot), measures of central tendency and their types. Applied biochemistry: Principles of nutrient metabolism, energy balance, fluid and electrolyte balance and acid–base regulation; their relevance to nutritional, metabolic and clinical disorders. Host–pathogen relationships, innate and acquired immunity, maternal immunity, vaccination and immunosuppression. Application of parasite life cycles to prevention and control.

topics.title: ANIMAL PRODUCTION, NUTRITION AND FARM MANAGEMENT
topics.detail: Livestock production systems: Smallholder and commercial dairy, beef, sheep, goat and camel production systems. Locally important breeds, production constraints and opportunities for improvement. Housing and husbandry: Housing, ventilation, stocking density, water supply, sanitation and animal comfort. Calf and young-stock rearing, milking management, lactation and dry-period management; maintenance of working animals. Poultry production: Broiler, layer and breeder management; hatchery hygiene, incubation, hatchability, chick quality, brooding, lighting, litter management and ventilation. Performance assessment: Milk yield and quality, growth, mortality, culling, reproductive efficiency, feed conversion, egg production and flock uniformity. Use of farm records and benchmarks to identify and resolve management problems. Nutritional principles: Functions of energy, protein, fibre, minerals, vitamins and water; digestion and nutrient utilisation in ruminants, monogastric animals and poultry. Balanced feeding: Requirements for maintenance, growth, reproduction and production; body-condition assessment and recognition of nutritional deficiencies and excesses. Simple ration evaluation using supplied feed-composition and requirement data. Fodder and feed resources: Locally available feeds, pasture management, seasonal fodder planning, hay, silage, crop residues and safe use of non-conventional feeds. Feeding management: Feeding of young, transition and lactating animals and poultry; prevention of feeding-related disorders, drought feeding and water security. Feed safety and efficiency: Sampling, quality assessment, adulteration, spoilage, mycotoxins and storage losses. Safe use of supplements, urea and additives; principles of probiotics, prebiotics and feed enzymes. Reduction of feeding costs and nutrient losses while maintaining health and productivity. Aquaculture: Basic production systems, water quality, stocking, feeding, biosecurity and recognition of fish mortality events; food-safety implications and integrated production systems. Wildlife and zoo animals: Principles of conservation, captive-animal health, quarantine, welfare and disease risks at wildlife–livestock interfaces.

children.title: Protozoa
children.detail: Protozoa: Locomotion and types of pseudopodia, reproduction and parasitic protozoans.

children.title: Porifera
children.detail: Porifera: Cellular organization, body wall, skeleton, and canal systems.

children.title: Cnidaria
children.detail: Cnidaria: Body wall, nematocysts, polymorphism, alternation of generations and coral reefs.

children.title: Platyhelminthes
children.detail: Platyhelminthes: Body wall, parasitic adaptations, and life cycles of some major groups (e.g., Fasciola hepatica, Taeniasolium).

children.title: Aschelminthes and Nematoda
children.detail: Aschelminthes and Nematoda:Pseudocoelomate organization, body wall, and life cycles of human parasitic nematodes (e.g., Hookworms, Pinworms, filarial worms).

children.title: Mollusca
children.detail: Mollusca: Modifications of foot, feeding mechanisms and predatory adaptations of cephalopods.

children.title: Annelida &Arthropoda
children.detail: Annelida &Arthropoda: Metamerism, tagmatization, mouthparts, ecdysis, metamorphosis, and ecological importance.

children.title: Echinodermata
children.detail: Echinodermata: Diversity; water vascular system, larval forms and development.

topics.title: Chordata: Introduction and General Organization
topics.detail: Origin, diagnostic characteristics and basic chordate body plan; major subdivisions of chordates, including proto-chordates and vertebrates.

topics.title: Fishes: Vertebrate Success in Water
topics.detail: Origin, diversity, classification and phylogenetic relationships of major fish groups. Structural and functional adaptations for aquatic life: swim bladder; respiration; excretion and osmoregulation.

topics.title: Amphibians: The First Terrestrial Vertebrates
topics.detail: Origin, classification and evolutionary relationships of amphibians. Structural, physiological and behavioral adaptations for aquatic and terrestrial life: Respiration, reproduction and development.

topics.title: Reptiles: The First Amniotes
topics.detail: Evolution of reptiles, adaptations for terrestrial life, excretion, osmoregulation, reproduction and development; Extinction of dinosaurs; poisonous apparatus and biting mechanism of snakes.

topics.title: Aves: Feathers, Flight and Endothermy
topics.detail: Evolutionary history and major adaptations associated with feathers, flight and endothermy. Structural and functional adaptations for aerial locomotion and respiration. Bird migration and navigation.

topics.title: Mammalia: Specialized Teeth, Hair, Endothermy and Viviparity
topics.detail: Origin, diversity and emphasis on major mammalian groups. Dentition in vertebrates. Comparative account of the evolution of the heart and vertebrate stomach. Temperature regulation and endothermy.

sections.title: PRINCIPLES OF LIFE AND GENERAL ZOOLOGY

topics.title: Cell and Molecular Biology
topics.detail: Comparative analysis of prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells. Structure and specialized functions of the nucleus, plasma membrane and cytoplasmic organelles. Enzyme structure, catalytic mechanisms, regulation, and inhibition. Major metabolic pathways: glycolysis, the Krebs cycle, and the electron transport chain. DNA as genetic material, structural organization of nucleic acids, the genetic code, transcription, and translation. Mitosis and meiosis, and their biological significance.

topics.title: Animal Form, Function and General Physiology
topics.detail: Vertebrate integument. Ultra-structure of muscle fibrils and mechanisms of muscle contraction. Regional functional organization of the gastrointestinal tract. Composition and functions of blood and internal fluids. Cardiovascular dynamics: electrical activity of the heart, cardiac output and blood pressure regulation. Comparative account of respiratory organs; properties and functions of respiratory pigments. Functional anatomy of the vertebrate nephron and urine formation. Mechanism of osmoregulation, and thermoregulation. Structural and functional units of the nervous system. Nerve impulse and its transmission. Structure and function of sensory organs (eye and ear). Endocrine glands, classes of hormones, mechanisms of hormone action.

topics.title: Genetics & Recombinant DNA Technology
topics.detail: Mendelian principles of inheritance, gene interactions, multiple alleles, linkage, crossing over and sex-linked inheritance. Eukaryotic chromosome structure; chromosomal aberrations, gene mutations, and the evolving gene concept. Recombinant DNA technology, cloning strategies, applications of genetic engineering, and transgenic animals.

topics.title: Evolutionary Biology
topics.detail: Theories of the origin of life. Darwinism and Neo-Darwinism. Causes of variation and types of natural selection. Genetic drift and Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium. Species concepts, mechanisms of speciation (allopatric, parapatric, sympatric), adaptive radiation, phylogeny and ontogeny.

topics.title: Environmental Biology & Ecology
topics.detail: Ecosystem concepts: components, primary/secondary productivity, trophic levels, food chains, food webs, and energy flow dynamics. Biogeochemical cycles (carbon, nitrogen). Environmental pollution (air, water, land), greenhouse effect, acid rain, global warming, climate change, and wildlife conservation and management.
